name: linux-service-start
title: Start a stopped enabled service
description: Starts one systemd service that is enabled at boot but not running (systemctl start). Units that are not enabled, and anything that is not a .service, are refused.
measure: props=$(systemctl show -p Id -p ActiveState -p Result -p Type -p RemainAfterExit -p ExecMainStartTimestampMonotonic -p ExecMainPID -p SuccessExitStatus -- "$unit" 2>/dev/null)
if [ "$enabled" != enabled ]; then arh_blocker "Only services enabled at boot are started here; $unit is ${enabled:-unknown}"; fi
# a one-shot is done only when it ran since boot and systemd counted that run a success. systemd starts every unit with Result=success and
# reset-failed sets it back, so ask how the run ended. First the journal: PID 1 logs the end of each run (unit succeeded, failed or skipped),
# and a record older than the run's main process is about an earlier run. systemd unloads an inactive unit nothing refers to, and with it
# the run (ExecMainStartTimestampMonotonic is 0 again), so then only the journal can tell. Without a record, the status of each command of
# the run: exit 0, an exit code or signal listed in SuccessExitStatus=, or a command marked "-" (ignore_errors=yes) is a success
if [ "$type" = oneshot ] && [ "$remain" = no ] && [ "$state" = inactive ] && [ "$result" = success ]; then

cmds=$(systemctl show -p ExecCondition -p ExecStartPre -p ExecStart -p ExecStartPost -p ExecStop -p ExecStopPost -- "$unit" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^\(Exec[A-Za-z]*\)={ .* ; ignore_errors=\([a-z]*\) ; start_time=\[[^]]*] ; stop_time=\[[^]]*] ; pid=\([1-9][0-9]*\) ; code=\([a-z]*\) ; status=\([0-9]*\)\/*\([A-Z0-9+]*\) }$/\1 \2 \3 \4 \5 \6/p')
while read -r kind ignore cpid how st sig; do
killed:*) case " $okexit " in *" $sig "*|*" SIG$sig "*) ;; *) bad=yes ;; esac ;;
if [ "$main" = yes ] && [ "$bad" = no ]; then finished=yes; fi
if [ "$state" = active ]; then arh_plan false "Already running"
elif [ "$finished" = yes ]; then arh_plan false "Ran and finished (a one-shot service)"
